text:
sara: Heads-up - after the LL128 rollout on the p4 cluster we see ~12% throughput regression on 2k-token generation workloads. latency tails up too. reverting LL128 on canary removes the regression.

mike: hmm, is this only when reduce-chunking is enabled? we turned that on in the same rollout.

sara: yes looks correlated. LL128 + reduce-chunking + small KV prefetches seems particularly bad.

anil: can you paste perf numbers and the allreduce profile?

sara: perf test (avg tokens/s): ll64+rc: 1100, ll128+rc: 970, ll128 (no rc): 1120. tail p99 latency: ll64+rc 210ms, ll128+rc 270ms.

sara: profiler snippet from nvprof-like sampling (top stack for stall):
```
allreduce_kernel(size=16KB): 1.8ms 
allreduce_kernel(size=2KB): 0.5ms (called x20)
kernel_exec_time_total: 45ms
comm_wait_total: 28ms
```

mike: that pattern screams high call-count for small allreduces. reduce-chunking splits bigger ops? or kv prefetch triggers many tiny reductions.

leo: reproduced locally on 4xA100 with microbench. With LL128 and channels=2 we see higher enqueue overhead vs LL64 for lots of small fragments. channels=4 lowered latency for big ops but increased small-op contention.

anil: what's NCCL config? envs?

sara: current: 
```
NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0
NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=2
NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
```

sara: CI perf-run attached: job 2026-07-12_06: perf regression on branch. @ci-bot flagged it as perf-fail.

ci-bot: perf-check: FAIL (throughput -11.8% vs baseline). See artifacts: /ci/artifacts/2026-07-12/1912345678/perf.zip

mike: quick experiment idea: try NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE or ALGO=TREE for small fragments, or bump threshold to force LL64 for small comms. Also try disable reduce-chunking to see if that avoids splitting into many small collects.

anil: also KV prefetch currently issues prefetch per attention head shard; maybe we can coalesce KV prefetches per-layer to reduce number of allreduces. batching heuristic could aggregate small prefetches within a 2ms window.

leo: I ran three microconfigs overnight:
- base (ll64, rc on): throughput 1125 tokens/s
- ll128 + rc: 980 tokens/s
- ll128 + rc + NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE: 1088 tokens/s
So SIMPLE proto recovers most of the loss.

mike: interesting. suggests LL128 impl + proto=LL128 has higher per-call latency for small buffers. SIMPLE uses a different codepath that handles many small collects better.

anil: for short-term mitigation: set NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE in deployment manifest for the heavy-small-prefetch pools, and open issue to add an adaptive proto selector in runtime (pick proto based on median allreduce size distribution).

leo: filed issue 4567 with profiler traces and experiment logs. Also added a per-model config knob to force proto/algos.

devops: rolling an emergency canary to change NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE on canary pool now. ETA 10m.

sara: thanks. two follow-ups: (1) adjust batching heuristic to coalesce KV prefetch within 1-2ms window; (2) runtime to emit histogram of allreduce sizes so we can auto-select proto.

mike: agree. I'll prototype a histogram + simple heuristic in the runtime: if median_allreduce_size < 8KB -> proto=SIMPLE, else proto=LL128.

anil: also let's add a regression test that runs our 2k-token config under LL128+rc and asserts no >5% drop vs baseline. Catch it in CI before rollout.

sara: perfect. I'll monitor canary once devops finishes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
